tagline: Up the west bank on the old Middlesex Turnpike.
intro: Route 154 comes up from Chester into Haddam and keeps to the west bank of the Connecticut River for nine miles, sharing the road with Route 82 for a stretch, past Haddam Meadows and on through Higganum to the Middletown line.

From 1802 to 1876 this was the Middlesex Turnpike, a toll road from Old Saybrook to Wethersfield. Haddam is the only town in Connecticut the river cuts down the middle, and for its first two hundred years the river was its living. Wallace Stevens gave the place a line of verse, addressed to its thin men.

moments.title: Haddam Meadows State Park
moments.text: Given in 1944 by the Hazen Foundation, the park's 175 acres hold meadow and hardwoods, marsh, a beach and a sand bar on the river.

moments.title: Higganum
moments.text: The natural cove at Higganum Landing was a river port and shipyard from the late 1700s to the mid-1800s, and the village green now keeps a shad museum.
